gpt.rationale: For nonpayment of rent, a tenant is guilty of detainer only after default and service of a written three-day notice requiring payment of the rent or possession of the property. Therefore, the landlord must give three days’ notice before filing the eviction action for nonpayment.

gemini.rationale: South Dakota law requires a landlord to give a tenant a three-day written notice to quit or pay the rent due before filing an eviction action. This notice can be served after the rent has been due and unpaid for three days, as specified in SDCL § 21-16-1(4).

pay_or_quit.description: Nonpayment of rent — South Dakota has no statutory pay-or-quit notice requirement for nonpayment. SDCL §21-16-2, which formerly provided notice procedures, was repealed by SB 90 (2024). Under SDCL §21-16-1(4), a forcible entry and detainer cause of action for nonpayment arises after the rent is 3 days past due (the 3-day ripening period). No advance written notice is required before filing. Attorney confirmed: Andy Cohen, 2026-06-19.

federal.name: SCRA § 3951 (Servicemembers Civil Relief Act)
federal.applies_when: Servicemembers and their dependents occupying a residence as their primary dwelling, where the servicemember's military service materially affects their ability to pay the rent.
federal.effect: During a period of military service, a landlord may not evict a servicemember or their dependents from their primary residence without first obtaining a court order. Court may stay proceedings up to 90 days or adjust the rental obligation. Protection applies when monthly rent does not exceed the annual threshold: $4,954.34/month (2024; formula: 130% of BAH for E-5 with dependents, highest BAH area — adjusted annually by DoD). Landlord must file affidavit of non-military-service before default judgment may enter (50 U.S.C. § 3931(b)(1)). FY23 NDAA amendment: replaced CPI-adjusted fixed-dollar threshold with current BAH formula.

holdings.statutory_note: South Dakota’s retaliatory-eviction protection for residential tenants is statutory, principally under SDCL §§ 43-32-27 and 43-32-28, which prohibit specified landlord retaliation—such as seeking possession, increasing rent, or decreasing services—because a tenant complained about housing-code or habitability issues or engaged in tenant-organization activity, subject to statutory exceptions.
